subject: Character portrait, three-quarter-length figure from head to hip, centred with clear headroom and composed to fill a square frame, eye level, shallow depth of field. A charid woman in her thirties, one of the fae, and the coolest thing in a warm room. Her skin is not coloured but translucent: pale as thin porcelain with a cold blue cast lying beneath the surface, so light passes through the rim of her ear and the web of her thumb, and the blood reads blue-violet rather than red at the lip and under the nail. Her skin never takes the colour of the light falling on it -- the oil lamp has turned the whole room and everyone in it warm amber, and she alone stays cold blue-white and lit from within, as though a different and colder light sat behind her face. Her skin must never look yellow, sallow, olive, golden or jaundiced, and must never look like blue or purple paint. She is human in every feature, ordinary in build, about five foot three. Hair an ordinary dark colour. Eyes deep amber, level, held a beat longer than is comfortable. Black silk with jet at the collar, a season or two behind the fashion, gloves off and set on the table. She sits at a small table in a dim subscription room, half-turned away and looking back at the viewer over her shoulder with a glass in her hand, the oil lamp set behind her and to one side so that it rims her and does not flood her face. Attentive. No wings of any kind. No text or lettering anywhere in the image.
prompt:
Aetherpunk gaslit dark fantasy of the early-1900s industrial era. Character portrait composed to fill a square frame with the head high and clear headroom. Vary the pose between portraits: subjects may face left or right regardless of sex, turn toward or away from the viewer, stand square on, glance over a shoulder, lean against something, sit, or be caught mid-occupation. Avoid giving every subject the same three-quarter turn and the same level stare. A painted illustration and never a photograph: oil-painted concept art with visible brushwork, soft painterly edges, and passages where detail dissolves into suggestion rather than being resolved. Dramatic and richly rendered, with deep chiaroscuro, near-black shadow and volumetric haze. Light is sparing and motivated: one or two large, clearly sourced pools falling on the subject, with the surroundings mostly unlit and dissolving into dark. Avoid scattered golden glints, speckled specular highlights, sparkle, glitter and bloom -- background brass, glass and metal stay dull and unlit rather than catching a hundred small lights. Avoid photographic realism, lens bokeh, pore-level skin detail and any camera artifact. Scenes are lit chiefly by gaslight, coal-fire and candle. Aetherium violet appears only where the setting genuinely warrants it -- a lamp, tube, coil or vessel -- and when it appears it is a true light source casting real light, used sparingly as a restrained counterpoint and never the dominant color of the image. Period dress across all classes: flat caps, waistcoats, wool coats, aprons, shawls and work clothes for laboring folk; tailored coats, starched collars, silks, jet, brocade and fine embroidery for patricians, old houses and the undying. A subject's own house colors may be rich and saturated in their garments while the environment stays coal grey, soot black, tarnished brass and verdigris. Render non-human folk with their features plainly visible -- horns, tails, fur, scales, beaks, tusks, unusual eye and skin color. Keep period silhouettes: no modern clothing, no plate armor, no wizard robes, no glowing weapons, no text or lettering.
